name: Hypefury
tagline: Draft and schedule text-led social posts with reusable queues
verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Hypefury, draft and schedule text-led social posts with reusable queues. The hard boundary is platform integrations, auto-reposting, cross-posting, analytics, and creator templates, plus api access, connector upkeep, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Draft and schedule text-led social posts with reusable queues, preview them accurately, publish through one official API, and retain a searchable content calendar.
requirements: developer application for one social network
whatYouLose: platform integrations, auto-reposting, cross-posting, analytics, and creator templates
moatNotes: API access, connector upkeep, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Hypefury because the scheduler is easy; staying approved and correct across constantly changing social APIs is the subscription. The recurring cost buys OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Active open-source social media scheduling platform.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: Drafts, schedules and repeatable publishing across networks; the growth-hack buttons are absent.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or clone the repository and deploy with Docker Compose or a supported PaaS.
facts.engines: No model is bundled; its REST API and MCP server connect external agents such as Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor or custom clients.
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in BrightBean's cloud; self-hosted data uses PostgreSQL 16+ with media on local disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: BrightBean omits Hypefury's X-specific growth automations such as auto-plugs, promotion rules and creator playbooks.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting social networks requires first-party platform developer/OAuth credentials; self-hosting also requires Docker or a PaaS.

alternatives.name: Fedica Free
alternatives.desc: Text-first cross-posting with a ten-item live queue; useful forever, provided your ideas arrive in batches of ten.

facts.install: Hosted signup and OAuth connection to each social account.
facts.dataFormat: Connected profiles, drafts, scheduled posts, media and analytics live in Fedica's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: Fedica provides basic text scheduling but not Hypefury's evergreen growth automations, and only ten items can wait in the queue.

alternatives.name: Mixpost Lite
alternatives.desc: Evergreen queues and scheduled posts without the X-growth theatre; Docker is compulsory.

facts.install: Docker Compose is recommended; a manual Laravel/Composer installation is also documented.
facts.dataFormat: MySQL stores application data, Redis handles queues/cache, and media uses local/public disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Mixpost can recycle queued posts but lacks Hypefury's X-specific growth, promotion and monetization automations.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server with Docker plus social-platform app credentials; the manual path also needs PHP, Composer, Supervisor, cron, Redis and FFmpeg.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: Threads, scheduling and recurring posts across many networks; the server stack is the recurring part you keep.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting.
facts.engines: Optional AI/media features connect to OpenAI, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Tavily, KieAI and Transloadit.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL holds application data; Redis and Temporal support jobs; media is stored locally or in Cloudflare R2/S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Postiz handles recurring publishing but not Hypefury's creator-growth playbooks, and it adds a server stack to maintain.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is straightforward; self-hosting requires Docker, social OAuth apps, and a PostgreSQL, Redis and Temporal stack.

alternatives.name: TryPost
alternatives.desc: Drafts, calendar, automations and twelve-network publishing; AI help costs whatever model you connect.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or production Docker Compose; a bare-metal installation is also documented.
facts.engines: AI writing can use OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the deployment template also exposes Anthropic and Gemini keys.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL or MySQL stores app data, Redis handles queues/cache, and media is local or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: TryPost is a broad social scheduler rather than an X growth system, so Hypefury's auto-promotion and creator-specific automations are absent.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs a SQL database, Redis, media storage, and separate developer credentials for each social platform.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Standard plan and a single-network scheduler DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Hypefury in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and one official social-platform API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: draft and schedule text-led social posts with reusable queues, preview them accurately, publish through one official API, and retain a searchable content calendar.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support drafts, scheduled times, queues, campaigns, tags, and a weekly calendar.
Connect exactly one social network using its documented OAuth flow.
Validate character, media, aspect-ratio, and file-size limits before scheduling.
Publish through an idempotent background job with retries and clear failure states.
Store platform post identifiers and refresh publication status without scraping.
Add reusable snippets, local media storage, CSV export, and a token reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out unofficial automation or scraping.
Deliberately leave out multi-network inbox and social listening.
Deliberately leave out agency approvals, white labelling, and enterprise reporting.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
